events: The first Book of Common Prayer
Cranmer’s English liturgy replaces the Latin services.
The Elizabethan Settlement
The Acts of Supremacy and Uniformity restore the Prayer Book.
The Articles enforced
The Thirty-nine Articles appear in English. The clergy are required to subscribe to them.
Hooker’s Laws
The first four books of Of the Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity.
Hampton Court and the Canons
King James meets the bishops and the Puritans. The Canons of 1604 follow.
The King James Bible
Andrewes leads the Westminster company of translators.
Laud at Canterbury
William Laud becomes archbishop.
The war of pamphlets
Parliament impeaches the bishops. The presses are unlicensed and the Church argues in print.
Laud executed
The Directory for Public Worship replaces the Prayer Book.
The Act of Uniformity
It enforces the Prayer Book of 1662. Some two thousand ministers leave their livings.
The Seven Bishops
Sancroft and six bishops are tried and acquitted. James II flees.
The Nonjurors deprived
Sancroft, Ken, Turner and others refuse the oaths to William and Mary.
The Oxford Movement
Keble’s Assize Sermon and the first Tracts for the Times.
Tract 90
Newman reads the Articles in a catholic sense. Pusey defends him.

names.bio: James Ussher (1581–1656), Archbishop of Armagh, chronologer and patristics scholar. He was the most learned churchman of the Stuart age.

One of the most respected English casuists of his century; Izaak Walton wrote his Life. As Regius Professor of Divinity at Oxford he gave the Latin praelectiones on the obligation of conscience, steering between Roman manuals and Puritan scrupulosity. They shaped Anglican moral theology's use of natural law. He later became Bishop of Lincoln.
